items.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq sink on hot inflation, new Trump tariffs as chip rout continues
items.take: Wall Street is opening with everything it feared at once: hotter inflation, fresh tariff threats and a chip rout that will not let up, and the Dow is down roughly 800 points early. Monday's Nvidia relief rally is now fully unwound, and the tape goes into the Thanksgiving holiday deep red.

items.title: Stocks tumble as AI sell-off deepens, Fed's preferred inflation gauge rises
items.take: Nvidia fell 5.1% premarket after dropping 5.9% Tuesday, with AMD down 6.5%, Micron and Marvell about 6%, echoing a 3.1% slide across chip-heavy Asia-Pacific markets. The brief relief sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement evaporated in a single day.

items.title: 5 Things Investors Need to Know About Wednesday's Markets
items.take: Core PCE, the Fed's preferred gauge, rose to 3.3% versus the 3.2% expected, cementing bets on a December hike now priced at 98% odds. Consumer confidence, durable goods and the Fed's Beige Book all land today, the last full data day before the holiday.

items.title: US stock market crash: what is driving Wall Street's brutal sell-off?
items.take: Trump's proposed 20% tariffs on 14 trading partners, including India, China, Japan and the EU, landed on top of the inflation surprise and the chip unwind. Three shocks at once is how a bad week turns into a red week before the December 9 Fed decision.

items.title: Nvidia stock continues to fall after massive rally, Jensen Huang apologizes to employees
items.take: The exuberance around Huang's return faded inside 48 hours and he opened his first day back apologizing to employees, even as Anthropic slid 8% back below its IPO price and Oracle dropped more than 8%. The AI trade's problem was never the CEO chair.
